[url=https://www.redbubble.com/people/elfgamesworks/shop]ElfGamesWorks Shop[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35453367/334f3a4bdb541ca7e6e74d0818a4e0ff88ea5cbf.png[/img]

Last but not least, the bugfixes:
- [BLOCKING] Using an item on a character and holding the left mouse button while hovering the item menu can break the sequence and softlock the player.
- Tiny teleport area causes the player to get lost in the third layer of the forest trunk area

notes.title: Patch 1.1.4. in time for Summer Sale!
notes.content:
Hello adventurers!

Can you believe it's already been a thrilling six months since we released Children of Silentown? 🎂🎉 Time really does fly when you're having fun and patching up game bugs, eh?

We want to express our gratitude to everyone for being with us on this journey. Your feedback, discussions, and enthusiasm have been the driving force behind our ongoing commitment to improving the game.

But hold on, we've got some scorching hot news for you! 🔥 The game is currently on discount for the Summer Sales! So, if you have friends who haven't yet had the chance to explore Silentown and solve its mysteries, there's no better time than now! Let them know, alright? 😉

Moving on to the updates, we're pleased to announce the release of patch 1.1.4. This update addresses several issues related to the Second Run / New Game feature:

[list]
[*] [BLOCKING] Firewood chest was open from the beginning when furball sticker was already in the inventory. This issue has now been resolved.
[*] Fixed Thibescus in the islands couldn't be taken: Those elusive Thibescus should now be able to be picked up as intended.
[*] Barn items couldn't be taken. Same issue, same solution :D
[/list]

Before we sign off, remember to keep sharing your thoughts and feedback with us. Every bit of it helps us to make the game better for all of you!

Stay cool during the summer and happy gaming!

Warm regards,
Elfs

notes.title: Chapter Select on NG+ available in branch!
notes.content:
Hello hello!

Our launch week is almost over, and what week it was! 🔥🔥🔥

Many thanks again to everyone who has played the game, and special thanks for all the feedback!! 🎶😸

We are hard at work to fix bugs and issues, but also reading reviews and comments to see what QoL improvements people need the most… one of which is “Chapter Select on NG+”: we deployed this feature on a branch, so if you are interested go and check it out!

Branch name: 'experimental-public'
Password: none

“How to” for how Branches work: https://www.technipages.com/how-to-opt-into-a-game-beta-on-steam

Notes:
[list]
[*] The feature works on saves where you reached the ending at least once (NG+)
[*] The feature is not fully tested, so we will rely on your help to make it better 😀
[*] [b]We strongly suggest to make a backup of your save files[/b]
You can find them at: 
C:\Users\[YOUR_NAME]\AppData\LocalLow\Daedalic Entertainment GmbH\ChildrenOfSilentown
[*] Hopefully you will not encounter bugs, but you might - reach out in case.
[*] Due to how the game works, you will not be able to obtain the “Friend” achievement using Chapter Select, that is the only achievement that requires to fully replay the game.
[/list]


Thank you!
Elfs


PS: our launch discount is almost over, it should end around 6 pm GMT+1 on Wednesday. If you want to recommend the game to a friend, now’s the time!!

PPS: did you figure out how to obtain the “Friend” achievement? It might not be the easiest!

notes.title: Children of Silentown is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
Heyho everyone!

It has been an exciting development cycle ... but we are delighted to announce that today is the day! Our new point&click adventure Children Of Silentown releases TODAY!

[previewyoutube=892bSi29lo0;full][/previewyoutube]

It is finally time for you to get this traditional point&click adventure with modern features, well balanced puzzles and mini games, and a mystery that needs solving! Enjoy the most beautiful soundtrack while exploring this delightfully drawn, Burtonesque world and take in its both wholesome yet eerie vibes.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Developer Spotlight
notes.content:
Heyho everone,

Today, Elf Games and Luna2 are shedding light on how Children of Silentown came to be. 
Insights about the unique design of the game as well many more infos are now available in this developer spotlight:

[previewyoutube=y6aNdGfEhws;full][/previewyoutube]

Originally developed as an animated short, Elf Games and Luna2 collaborated to bring the Children of Silentown into the interactive medium. The Making Of video tells the tale of how this suggestion snowballed into the game we see today as a full-fledged title, made by this small group of people in their off-hours from their full-time jobs in software development and full-time content creation on YouTube. 

As we (Daedalic) can testify from first hand experience - the passion this team is spreading is infectious - and if you already feel the same, there is a whole prologue of the game for you to get your hands on to ease the wait until [b]Children of Silentown releases on January 11th[/b]

notes.title: Release Date Announcement
notes.content:
[b]Heyho everyone,[/b]

We’re super excited to announce the release date for Children of Silentown – a dark adventure set in a mysterious community that’s surrounded by an ominous forest. On January 11th, 2023, you’ll be able to discover the secrets hidden within!

[previewyoutube=Jn1aic0Z2r0;full][LINK][/previewyoutube]

Children of Silentown is a dark point-and-click adventure game that follows Lucy, a girl growing up in a village deep in a forest inhabited by monsters, as she slowly begins unravelling the mysteries surrounding her. The unique hand-drawn and eerie art style combined with atmospheric music builds a hauntingly beautiful world for you to explore, solve puzzles and play minigames in, as you slowly peel away the layers of mystery surrounding Lucy’s nightmares and the forest just outside of town.

You’ll be collecting and combining items to solve puzzles, but you’ll also be learning songs to communicate with others and progress through the game, with these songs, you’ll be able to shape and influence Lucy’s story, which will lead to multiple different endings.

If you’re interested to already get a small glipmse into the story, there is a free Prologue available:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1451740/Children_of_Silentown_Prologue/

notes.title: TRY OUR DEMO at the Steam Game Festival!
notes.content:
Howdy!

This demo is meant to give you a taste of the world of Children of Silentown, our dark adventure game scheduled for release for late 2020.

Inspired by point & click games like Fran Bow, and with an art style reminiscent of “Coraline” and Tim Burton’s early works, Children of Silentown tells the story of Lucy amidst the horror of people disappearing, monsters, and an isolated village surrounded by forest.

Only by taking advantage of all the tools and tricks at her disposal, Lucy will be able to shed some light on the mysteries of Silentown, using her singing skills to tear the veil of apathy and silence surrounding the village.

Follow Lucy through her adventure between puzzles, minigames and important choices leading to different endings!

We released a first trailer back in 2019 that was quite well-received, also thanks to the superbly animated video by our collaborator and YouTuber Fraffrog (1M followers, go check her out!). Now the game is at the point where we can proudly show a nice, well-designed and super-polished demo, reason why we would like you to have a taste during this Steam Game Festival. :)

[h2]ABOUT US[/h2]
Elf Games is a small indie developer from Brescia, Italy. 
Our first game, Little Briar Rose, is a vibrant and colorful adventure inspired by the tale of Sleeping Beauty and her enchanted forest of brambles. With Children of Silentown we are delving into the dark side of fables (and forests!) with a creepy, unsettling story… which we hope you’ll like!

Thanks
Elfs


PS: if you play the demo… give us some feedback, will ya?! Something not working? Something you didn’t like? Let us hear the details!  :*

PPS: If that’s ok with you, please follow our developer page to get updates on all our games: https://store.steampowered.com/developer/ElfGamesWorks

PPPS: Adding a third “PS” only for fashion. Wizardry fashion. Does it ring a bell?

notes.title: Devlog #1 – 10K views and our “secret” to animations!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
🎉 Woohoo, the reveal trailer for Children of Silentown hits 10K views on YouTube! 🎉

Thank you all for all the interest, the support and the love!

If you haven’t already, give it a look, smash that “like” button and… WISHLIST NOW!

[url]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1108000/Children_of_Silentown/[/url]

Also, it’s time for a small update! 

We are currently working on the animations and the expressiveness of our cute female protagonist.

To animate the characters of Children of Silentown (CoS for friends) we use an animation technique called “bone animation”, consisting of associating our characters’ graphics to a skeleton, and then moving it. This technique allows us to obtain incredibly smooth and fluid animations, opening up to many possibilities. 

For our 2D animations, we use a program called Spine, which we had a chance to try out before and is now working very well for us in CoS. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33027633/119f18f1e1a23d5208c48aee102a62b10faa1785.gif[/img]

But how does it work?

To create a character and it’s animations, we first split the character’s body into several parts – such as head, arms, legs, and torso – and save them as separate images. Each piece is then associated with one or more bones and, possibly, a mesh. The bones are used to move the pieces of graphics and they are influenced by the other bones. Just like a wooden puppet.

The mesh, on the other hand, makes it possible to deform the graphics. It can be tightened, crumpled or stretched. This, in particular, is very useful to prevent the pieces of the body from appearing disjointed from one another. Basically, the wooden puppet from before has now a spandex suit on it (a bit kinky, I know).

Once this part is finished, we have our character back in one piece and in Setup Pose.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33027633/84c3da1332d01a3f9b200c4a6dd6c54dd324b97c.gif[/img]

Then we move into the animation itself. This is the point where we move further away from traditional, “puppet” animation. The keyword is: [b]interpolation[/b].

Assigning to every bone a “starting point” and an “arrival point”, Spine will complete and “fill in the gaps” of the animation for us. Since the software connects starting and arrival points with a straight line, the first iterations will probably look very rough and unnatural – but that’s only the start! With a little bit of patience, by adding more and more details the animation will improve immensely. 

As mentioned before, this is a very different approach from the one of traditional animation, but once you get the hang of the program and of how to make it work, the experience with classic animation will be fundamental to make the characters come alive.

At the end of the whole process, the animations are then imported into the game. Here’s how they look once everything’s ready:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33027633/1f2e72bb2cf180e132808c415bfbd0f8451824bd.gif[/img]

Once we’ve set up all the main, basic animations, we focus on trying to express the character feelings and mood through small gestures and expressions. Given the game’s peculiar style, a big part of the personality and behavior of the characters is defined through body language alone, so this is definitely something we want to focus on to give life to our characters and, ultimately, to our story.

This technique is helping us a lot give depth to our characters and fully take advantage of the creepy design style of our little adventure.

That’s all for now, stay tuned for the next blog post! 

Cheers,
Elfs
